races.title: State House, District 64
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Dennis Riddell
cands.bio: Republican who represented North Carolina House District 64 (southern Alamance County) from 2013 and lost re-election in 2026. Marine engineering graduate, Merchant Marine engineering officer, Naval Reserve veteran, former high school teacher, and owner of two local businesses. Former Alamance County GOP chairman.
cands.gaps: We could not find his birthplace, where he grew up, or when he moved to North Carolina. We found no documented stance on data centers, development or growth, and no statements on immigration or H-1B, guns, abortion, school choice or teacher pay, policing, or foreign or big-donor money. We found no bills he sponsored, since Ballotpedia's sponsored-legislation table was empty on the page we read. No endorsements for the 2026 race were identified, and no controversies turned up in the pages we had. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Served in the NC House from 2013 to 2026, including as vice chair of Appropriations. Also a Merchant Marine engineering officer for more than 30 years, a high school social studies teacher, and owner of FreedomIR Thermal Imaging and Heritage Stables Equestrian Facility. Chaired the Alamance County Republican Party for five years.
qual.why: About 13 years of prior legislative service and budget-writing work, plus business ownership, put him in the high band. No law or formal policy career is documented, and committee chair roles were not counted.
qual.label: About 13 years of prior legislative service and budget-writing work, plus business ownership, put him in the high band. No law or formal policy career is documented, and committee chair roles were not counted.

end-homestead-tax.evidence: His campaign website says he supports meaningful property tax relief to keep more money in residents' pockets and protect longtime homeowners from being priced out, and calls for greater accountability in how tax dollars are spent. It names no specific bill or elimination proposal.

prio.label: Matches 1 of 1 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 1 only promised (needs 2 to score)

cands.name: LeVon Barnes
cands.bio: Educator and coach, born in Staten Island, NY. Physical education teacher with Durham Public Schools, formerly head men's basketball coach and associate dean of students at Lackawanna College. Lost 2017 Durham City Council, 2020 county commissioner and 2024 NC House bids. Won NC House District 64 in 2026.

endorsements.text: 2026: Listed by Ballotpedia as endorsed or recommended by the Center for Freethought Equality, Work For Democracy, and several Sway voting groups (including NC Public School Champions and YALLvote).
2017 (Durham City Council run): endorsed by Equality NC, People for the American Way Next Up Fund, Run for Something, Sierra Club and VoteProChoice.

cands.gaps: We could not find when LeVon Barnes moved to North Carolina, so his ties to the state could not be scored. He had no elected office before winning this seat, so there is no record of official actions to report. We found no stated positions on homestead property taxes, restrictions on out-of-state or institutional land buyers, gun policy, or H-1B or current immigration enforcement. We also found no pledge on refusing particular kinds of donations. His 2024 Ballotpedia survey and campaign pages give stated positions only, not actions. We found no documented controversies, foreign ties or notable organizational endorsements beyond the voting-group and advocacy-group listings.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Career educator (PE teacher with Durham Public Schools, about 24 years), former college head basketball coach and associate dean of students, and adjunct instructor. He has not held elected office before this win; he ran unsuccessfully for Durham City Council (2017), Durham County commissioner (2020) and NC House (2024).
qual.why: He has no prior legislative or elected service and no law, policy or budget career in the record. His administrative and coaching roles show some management experience, but education is not directly tied to writing law and budgets.
qual.label: He has no prior legislative or elected service and no law, policy or budget career in the record. His administrative and coaching roles show some management experience, but education is not directly tied to writing law and budgets.

stop-data-centers.evidence: His campaign site says Alamance should prioritize small farms and businesses over a data center, and proposes to tax and regulate data centers so communities get benefits without the adverse effects. This is regulation, not a ban.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: His campaign site proposes state audits of development proposals to prevent rampant development that drains groundwater, and common-sense zoning policies worked out with local officials.

pro-life.evidence: His campaign site pledges to protect abortion access and reproductive healthcare in state law and to safeguard IVF and maternal care.

back-police-order.evidence: His campaign site pledges to oppose constitutional amendments that would hamper funding for law enforcement, and to fund mental health and PTSD recovery programs for officers and de-escalation training.

workers-first.evidence: His 2017 Durham City Council campaign site said the city should not cooperate with ICE, should protect DACA residents and should act on its sanctuary-city declaration.

prio.label: Matches 3 of 5 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 3 only promised

land_positions.quote_or_summary: Campaign platform says Alamance 'deserves leadership that prioritizes you and your business over a data center' and calls for taxing and regulating data centers so communities receive benefits without adverse health and quality-of-life effects.
Campaign platform proposes state audits of development proposals to prevent rampant development that drains groundwater and vital resources, plus common-sense zoning policies.
